title: Punctual purity and regular closed pairs: two of three
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion between regular Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, locally of constant codimension $c$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Among the following conditions, any two imply the third:
(a) the supported Kummer map $A_Z\to i^!A_X(c)[2c]$ is an isomorphism;
(b) $Z$ is punctually pure;
(c) $X$ is punctually pure at every point of $i(Z)$.
The statement applies also to localizations of the pair.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.1.4 and 3.2.1--3.2.2, Proposition 3.2.3 and proof, printed pp.243--244 (pointwise Gysin composition and cone supported at a closed point).

proof.text: Work separately where $c$ is constant. At each $x=i(z)$ first work in an affine open neighbourhood of $x$, restricting the class by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]; the subsequent localization morphism to this affine neighbourhood is affine. For $z\in Z$, set $x=i(z)$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, and $d=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. The local closed pair is $i_z:S\hookrightarrow T$; its closed-point maps are $a:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow S$ and $b=i_za:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow T$. Localization is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], and regular by the local-ring characterization [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The local rings are regular local rings, so their dimensions are finite. By [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus], these closed immersions are regular; the codimensions of $a,i_z,b$ are $d,c,d+c$, respectively. In particular $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=d+c$ (apply its displayed dimension formula to the closed immersions, whose residue-field extensions are identities). Localization is locally ind-etale: [lem-weil-pbc-localization-colimit-principal-localizations] expresses its affine ring map as a filtered colimit of principal open localizations, which are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Thus [lem-per-ind-etale-closed-support-base-change] identifies the restriction of $i^!A_X$ with $i_z^!A_T$; on these bounded-below objects the exceptional $i^!$ of the class is the derived supported kernel used there, the closed-support adjoint of [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction], by the identification written out in Step 3. The class itself restricts to $\eta_{i_z}$ by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus].

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244, proof

proof.text:
Put $\eta=\eta_{i_z}:A_S\to i_z^!A_T(c)[2c]$. Under closed exceptional transitivity [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition], fundamental-class composition [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], with coefficient exponent $n=1$, gives
$$\eta_b=\bigl(a^!\eta(d)[2d]\bigr)\circ\eta_a,$$
where
$$A_{\kappa(z)}\xrightarrow{\eta_a}a^!A_S(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{a^!\eta(d)[2d]}b^!A_T(c+d)[2(c+d)].$$
Here the middle arrow means applying $a^!$ to $\eta$ and then twisting and shifting. Tate lines pull back and tensor compatibly by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; commuting a line with $a^!$ follows locally by trivializing that line, where both comparisons are the identity, and then gluing. Consequently $\eta_a$ and $\eta_b$ are exactly the two punctual-purity maps in (b) and (c), with no change of normalization or sign. The transitivity is the canonical right-adjoint one, not an arbitrary identification of its objects.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244, proof

proof.text: The point functor $a^!$ of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is, on $D^+$, the closed-support adjoint of [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction], a triangulated right derived functor. Indeed, for the compactification $(\mathrm{id},a)$ the compact-support functor of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] is the total derived direct image of the exact $a_*$, which is termwise $a_*$ since exact functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Its right adjoint sends $D^+$ to $D^+$ (compute on a bounded-below injective resolution), so by uniqueness of right adjoints its restriction to $D^+$ is the chosen $a^!$ of [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction], with the same counit; likewise for $i_z$ and $b$. That node derives the supported inverse image, whose underived adjunction is [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction]. Its abelian-sheaf adjunction restricts to $A$-modules: scalar multiplication acts on the kernel, and the adjunction sends $A$-linear maps to $A$-linear maps by naturality. Module sheaves have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] supplies bounded-below K-injective representatives. Thus [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] applies to this additive supported functor and shows that it preserves shifts and cone triangles. The cone of $\eta$ belongs to $D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, since both source and target do. By the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], a morphism of derived complexes is an isomorphism precisely when a cone is acyclic, that is, zero in the derived category. In particular, if $a^!\eta$ is an isomorphism and $C$ is a cone of $\eta$, then $a^!C=0$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244, proof

proof.text: Assume (a). Step 1 makes $\eta_{i_z}$ an isomorphism for every $z$, so the second arrow of Step 2 is an isomorphism: every functor preserves inverses, and twist and shift are equivalences. If (b) also holds, its first arrow $\eta_a$ is an isomorphism, hence so is $\eta_b$, proving (c). If instead (c) holds, $\eta_b$ is an isomorphism; composing it with the inverse of the second arrow proves that $\eta_a$ is an isomorphism. This proves (b). Both arguments apply at every point of $Z$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244, proof

proof.text: Assume (b) and (c). For every local pair of Step 1, the first arrow and the composite in Step 2 are isomorphisms. Thus the second arrow equals $\eta_b\eta_a^{-1}$ and is an isomorphism. Undoing the twist and shift gives that $a^!\eta_{i_z}$ is an isomorphism. If $C_z$ is a cone of $\eta_{i_z}$, Step 3 therefore gives $a^!C_z=0$. This conclusion uses purity only for the two closed-point maps, not purity of the pair we are proving.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244, proof

proof.text: We prove by strong induction on the finite integer $d\geq0$ that $\eta_{i_z}$ is an isomorphism for every regular local pair as in Step 1 satisfying (b) and (c), with $\dim S=d$. The induction ranges over all such pairs, not just one original scheme. Let $U=S\setminus\{z\}$ and let $v:U\hookrightarrow S$ be its open inclusion. For every point $t\in U$, localization at $t$ gives a pair of smaller closed-scheme dimension: every chain of primes ending in the prime of $t$ can be extended by the distinct maximal ideal of the local ring of $S$, so $\dim\mathcal O_{S,t}<d$. The localizations still satisfy (b) and (c), since their further local rings are the original local rings at those points. Step 1 identifies their class with the restriction of $\eta_{i_z}$. The induction hypothesis makes that restriction an isomorphism, so $C_z$ has zero stalk at every geometric point over $t$. Inverse image preserves these stalks [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], and derived stalk conservativity [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative], applied to the underlying abelian complexes (forgetting the $A$-structure is exact and commutes with $\mathcal H^i$), yields $v^*C_z=0$. For $d=0$ there is no proper generization in $S$, hence $U$ is empty and the same vanishing holds without invoking induction.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244, proof

proof.text:
Apply [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] to the closed point $a$ of $S$ and the open complement $v$. Its triangle, together with $v^*C_z=0$, gives
$$C_z\xrightarrow{\sim}a_*a^*C_z.$$
Write $E=a^*C_z$. The closed adjunction $a_*\dashv a^!$ of [lem-exc-closed-ambient], in its bounded-below form [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction] (the same $a^!$ as in Steps 3 and 5), and Step 5 imply
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C_z,C_z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(a_*E,C_z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E,a^!C_z)=0.$$
The identity of $C_z$ is therefore zero, which makes $C_z$ a zero object. Its cone triangle then shows that $\eta_{i_z}$ is an isomorphism. This proves the induction step and the base case at once. The argument spells out the source's assertion that extraordinary and ordinary restriction agree on a complex supported at the closed point; it needs neither constructibility nor excellence.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244, proof

proof.text: For the original pair, Steps 5--7 show that the restriction of $\eta_i$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ is an isomorphism for every $z\in Z$. Its map on the stalk at every geometric point over $z$ is therefore an isomorphism, by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] on $Z$ proves (a). Together with Step 4 this proves all three implications. The same proof starts with any localization of the pair, as Step 1 already works for localizations. No global bound on $\dim X$ or $\dim Z$ was used; only finite dimensions of the regular local rings enter the induction. For the empty closed subscheme (a) is the unique isomorphism between zero objects and (b),(c) are vacuous. In codimension zero the class is the open-and-closed restriction class, including the identity class, by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus].
